diffs.evidence: HTS221 datasheet DocID026333 Rev 5, Sec. 8: 'The Registers in 30h..3Fh address range contain calibration coefficients. Every sensor module has individual coefficients.' and Sec. 7: 'The relative humidity and temperature values must be computed by linear interpolation of current registers with calibration registers, according to Table 19'. The datasheet gives no fixed offset (the second reading's 0 is not a datasheet value). The model's 40.8125 is exactly the interpolation of its own simulated calibration registers: H0_rH_x2=66 -> 33 %rH, H1_rH_x2=154 -> 77 %rH, H0_T0_OUT=0xF830=-2000, H1_T0_OUT=0x2430=9264; slope 44/11264=0.00390625 per count, offset 33+2000*0.00390625=40.8125. The driver reads 0x30-0x3F and interpolates per chip, as the datasheet requires.

The 40.81 shown is the humidity measure's offset (the gate fell back to the first measure because no offset matched); the model's temperature measure (0x2A) has scale 0.015625 and offset 18.4375. Datasheet Sec. 8: 'T0 and T1 are the actual calibration temperature values multiplied by 8 ... Every sensor module has individual coefficients', with conversion by linear interpolation (Figure 9). No fixed offset exists in the datasheet. From the model's sim registers: T0_degC_x8=160 (MSB bits 0) -> 20 C, T1_degC_x8=24+(1<<8)=280 -> 35 C, T0_OUT=100, T1_OUT=0x0424=1060; slope 15/960=0.015625, offset 20-100*0.015625=18.4375. Consistent with the datasheet; the driver interpolates using each chip's own calibration.
